title: Geometry optimization of pristine graphene
action: Run variable-cell DFT geometry optimization of a graphene unit cell (two carbon atoms) using Quantum ESPRESSO with LDA exchange-correlation functional to obtain the equilibrium in-plane lattice constant and total energy.
description: This step computes the reference pristine graphene structure and its total energy, needed for formation energy evaluation.

title: Geometry optimization of symmetric graphane
action: Run variable-cell DFT geometry optimization of a symmetric graphane unit cell (two carbon atoms, two hydrogen atoms on the same side) using the same DFT methodology to obtain the equilibrium lattice constant, planar atomic coordinates, and total energy.
description: The symmetric phase (boat-like) is required for its zero-strain lattice constant and its energy landscape.

title: Geometry optimization of anti-symmetric graphane
action: Run variable-cell DFT geometry optimization of an anti-symmetric graphane unit cell (two carbon atoms, two hydrogen atoms on opposite sides) using the same DFT methodology to obtain the equilibrium lattice constant, out-of-plane corrugation, and total energy.
description: The anti-symmetric phase (chair-like) exhibits sp³ rehybridization and provides the corrugation and bond geometry.

title: Fixed-cell optimization of symmetric graphane at a=2.69 Å
action: Perform a fixed-cell DFT geometry relaxation of the symmetric graphane unit cell with the in-plane lattice constant fixed at a=2.69 Å (10% biaxial tensile strain relative to graphene) to obtain the total energy at that strain.
description: This strained configuration provides the formation energy under 10% tensile strain, which is one of the key headline quantities.

title: Fixed-cell optimization of anti-symmetric graphane at a=2.69 Å
action: Perform a fixed-cell DFT geometry relaxation of the anti-symmetric graphane unit cell with the in-plane lattice constant fixed at a=2.69 Å (10% biaxial tensile strain relative to graphene) to obtain the total energy at that strain.
description: This strained configuration provides the formation energy under 10% tensile strain for the anti-symmetric phase, one of the key headline quantities.

title: Collect geometric parameters
action: From the optimized structures of steps 1–3, extract the following quantities: lattice constant a of pristine graphene (Å), symmetric graphane (Å), and anti-symmetric graphane (Å); for anti-symmetric graphane also the out-of-plane corrugation (Å), C–C bond length (Å), C–C–C bond angle (°), and H–C–C bond angle (°). Write all values to geometric_parameters.json.
description: The collected structural parameters are the primary geometric results reported in the paper.
output_schema: JSON object with keys a_graphene (Å), a_sym (Å), a_asym (Å), corrugation_asym (Å), bond_length_C_C (Å), bond_angle_C_C_C (degrees), bond_angle_H_C_C (degrees).

title: Compute formation energies
action: Compute the formation energy E_f = E(graphane) - E(graphene) - E(H) per C–H pair for each graphane phase, using the total energies from steps 1–4 (and the new strained anti-symmetric run) and the reference energy of an isolated hydrogen atom. Report E_f for symmetric graphane at zero strain, anti-symmetric graphane at zero strain, symmetric graphane at the strained condition (a=2.69 Å), and anti-symmetric graphane at the strained condition (a=2.69 Å). Write these to formation_energies.json.
description: Formation energies quantify the binding strength and are the central headline quantities linked to strain engineering.
output_schema: JSON object with keys E_f_sym_0 (eV/CH), E_f_asym_0 (eV/CH), E_f_sym_strained (eV/CH), E_f_asym_strained (eV/CH).
